correctness.rationale: The conditioning leaves a uniform residual perfect matching. For N=2n-4>=4, one prescribed residual edge has probability 1/(N-1) and two disjoint residual edges have joint probability 1/[(N-1)(N-3)]. Exact enumeration of pair overlaps gives E[XY]=C/M+(AB-Q+C)/(M(M-2)); direct factorization yields the claimed four-cell covariance. The noncrossing specialization is manifestly nonnegative; the crossing sign criterion is exact. For strictly positive four-gap compositions, n=4 and n=5 have only the enumerated positive-part patterns, all negative; n=6 exhibits both signs. A standard-library checker tests every circular gap arrangement and marked pairing through n=7 (1710 cases and 866880 exact matching comparisons) plus 19149 independent rational algebra comparisons through N=28. The proof, not finite enumeration, establishes the unbounded result.

value.rationale: Crossing degrees of two prescribed vertices are natural local statistics of random circle graphs. A complete geometric covariance sign criterion shows noncrossing chords cannot be negatively correlated under fixed-endpoint conditioning, while crossing chords with nonempty intervening arcs can be both positively and negatively correlated already at n=6. The equality/inequality boundary is an explicit quadratic-imbalance test, and balanced negative dependence tends to -1/8 while an imbalanced family has positive covariance growing as k/4. These distinctions cannot be inferred from marginal degrees or only total crossing moments.
